title: Best Whynter Dehumidifier (2026): Discontinued — Buy This Instead
dek: Whynter's standalone dehumidifiers are all marked discontinued. Here's what that means for owners and shoppers, plus the in-production units that fill the gap.
description: Every standalone Whynter dehumidifier is now discontinued. See the full model list, the 2021 recall to check, and the best current replacements to buy.
intro: If you're shopping for a **Whynter dehumidifier**, there's an important catch: every standalone model we could find — from the 30-pint RPD-321EW to the 70-pint RPD-702WP — is marked "Discontinued," both on Whynter's own site and at third-party retailers. Whynter's dehumidifier category currently shows no active listings at all.

That leaves two practical paths. If you need a dedicated dehumidifier, buy an in-production unit with the same capacity and drainage your Whynter had. If you specifically want Whynter hardware, its only remaining humidity-control product is the dehumidify mode on a portable air conditioner. And if you're looking at a used Whynter, check it against a 2021 recall first. We'll walk through all three.
topPicksLead: For most people replacing a Whynter, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best substitute: the same 50-pint class as Whynter's popular models, currently in production, with a much bigger tank.

It's one of our most-recommended units across the site; see the full comparison in our [best 50-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.caption: Capacities as originally listed; older ratings predate the 2019 DOE test and run higher than today's numbers.

blocks.text: One sizing note: Whynter's 60- and 70-pint labels date from the older test procedure, which used hotter, wetter conditions. A current 50-pint unit under the 2019 DOE test is roughly comparable to a 70-pint unit under the old rules, so you rarely need to size up when replacing one.

We don't lab-test. We confirmed each Whynter model's status on the manufacturer's own pages and at independent retailers, cross-checked the CPSC recall record, and matched each discontinued unit to current models by capacity and drainage type using DOE ratings, ENERGY STAR data and manuals.
Then we leaned on owner reviews to choose replacements with consistent reliability records, so you're not trading one hard-to-support unit for another.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Whynter replacement

items.label: Match capacity, not the brand
items.text: Pick by pints and drainage. Remember that older Whynter ratings use the pre-2019 test, so a current 50-pint unit usually replaces a 60- or 70-pint Whynter. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps if you're unsure.

items.label: Keep the pump if you had one
items.text: If your Whynter drained through a pump to a sink or window, buy a pump model so your setup still works.

items.label: A real humidistat
items.text: Set-a-number control lets the unit cycle instead of running nonstop.

items.label: A clean recall record
items.text: Check any used unit's model number and manufacture date at CPSC.gov.

items.label: Proper disposal of the old unit
items.text: Dehumidifiers contain refrigerant and shouldn't go out with the trash. See [how to dispose of a dehumidifier](/guides/how-to-dispose-of-a-dehumidifier/).

blocks.text: In 2021, the CPSC announced a recall of roughly 2 million dehumidifiers made by New Widetech and sold under about 20 brand names, including Whynter, Amana, Danby, Edgestar, Friedrich, Haier and Honeywell. The units can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards.

items: **Whynter models named:** RPD-302W (30 pints), RPD-503SP (50 pints) and RPD-702WP (70 pints).
**What to do:** stop using an affected unit and contact New Widetech for the recall remedy.

blocks.title: The RPD-702WP question
blocks.text: The recalled RPD-702WP shares its model number with a later-listed Whynter unit, and public sources don't make clear whether they're the same design. If you own or are buying an RPD-702WP, check the manufacture date on the nameplate against the September 1, 2017 cutoff before plugging it in.

sections.heading: Should you keep running an old Whynter dehumidifier?

blocks.text: If your Whynter isn't on the recall list and still works, there's no urgent reason to replace it. Plenty of these units have years of life left with basic care. Use this quick checklist to decide:

items: **Check the recall first.** Find the model number and manufacture date on the nameplate, usually on the back or under the bucket. If it's an RPD-302W, RPD-503SP or RPD-702WP made before September 1, 2017, stop using it.

**Clean the filter and coils.** A clogged filter is the most common reason an older unit ices up or stops collecting water. Our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) walks through it.
**Compare with a hygrometer.** If the room never gets below about 55% even with the unit running nonstop, it's either undersized or losing capacity.
**Watch for warning signs.** A burning smell, scorched plug, tripped breakers or a compressor that clicks on and off rapidly mean it's time to retire it.
**Replace, don't repair, a failed compressor or pump.** On a discontinued model, parts are hard to find and a new unit costs less than most repairs.

blocks.text: When it does need replacing, our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide can help you rule out simple fixes first, and our lifespan guide explains [how long dehumidifiers usually last](/guides/how-long-do-dehumidifiers-last/).

Whynter no longer sells a standalone dehumidifier. For a direct replacement, buy the **Midea Cube 50** for bucket-style use or the **hOmeLabs HME1003** if you need a pump. If you want Whynter hardware, the **ARC-14S** portable air conditioner is the only option, and it's a cooling appliance first. Before using any secondhand Whynter, check it against the 2021 recall. For every active brand side by side, see our [dehumidifier brands guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/).

faqs.a: Not standalone ones. Every Whynter dehumidifier we found — the RPD-321EW, RPD-311DW, RPD-421EW, RPD-411WG, RPD-501WP, RPD-506EWP, RPD-551EWP, RPD-561EGP, RPD-621EW and RPD-702WP — is marked discontinued, and Whynter hasn't announced a replacement.

faqs.q: What is the best replacement for a Whynter dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a bucket model, the Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT), a current 50-pint-class unit with a large tank. For a pump model, the hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi, which drains itself to a sink or window.

faqs.q: Was there a Whynter dehumidifier recall?
faqs.a: Yes. The CPSC's 2021 New Widetech recall named three Whynter models — the RPD-302W, RPD-503SP and RPD-702WP — manufactured before September 1, 2017. They can overheat and pose fire and burn hazards.

faqs.q: How do I check if my Whynter dehumidifier is recalled?
faqs.a: Look at the nameplate for the model number and manufacture date. The recalled Whynter models are the RPD-302W, RPD-503SP and RPD-702WP made before September 1, 2017. You can confirm on CPSC.gov by searching for the New Widetech dehumidifier recall.

faqs.q: Can I still get parts or a manual for my Whynter dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Whynter's site still hosts pages for discontinued models, which is the best place to start for manuals and support. Washable filters and drain hoses are generic enough that many owners keep older units running, but if the compressor or a pump fails, replacing the unit is usually the better value.

faqs.q: Can the Whynter ARC-14S replace a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Only partly. It's a 14,000 BTU dual-hose portable air conditioner with a dehumidify mode. It works in a hot, humid room but removes less moisture than a dedicated dehumidifier and isn't suited to a cool, damp basement.
